questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted somewhere culturally not too far from Denmark, as well as somewhere with great nature and especially mountains.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy to find the needed information through KU, and later on UBC's own website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any personal assistance, but most things had been sorted from home, and once at campus it was quite easy to figure out what to do.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I didn't need any specific assistance, but it seemed to be quite easy to get in touch with someone if you needed help.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of housing opportunities on campus, and usually exchange students are put together in housing like Walter Gage, Saltwater residence or Fairview.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
There were some meal plans available, but i never used them. 
All housing have kitchens, either shared between 4-6 people, or alone if you have a studio. There are no cooking utensils, so if your roomies don't have anything they will share with you, you have to buy your own! Also, when it comes to roomies you have to have an open mind since they are often quite young (between 18 and 20 years old), and usually haven't lived alone before - but that being said, you can definitely be lucky and meet some great new people.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is super convenient to live on campus, since everything you need is super close (uni, supermarket, fitness center, restaurants etc.). But the houses are very old and worn down, so don't expect anything fancy, even though you do pay quite a lot to live on campus. Also, it takes about 50 minutes to get downtown by bus, so be aware that you don't end up staying at campus all the time - there are so many nice places to see around Vancouver.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When accepted to study at UBC you first have to fill out a list of 10 possible courses, but this is not your final courses. Once the registration opens, you find all of the courses online and can manually change some of them if needed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You were able to write the UBC student services, which was super helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not a lot is written in the course description, so remember that during the add-and-drop phase in the first 2 weeks of the semester, you are allowed to switch courses if they turn out to be different than expected! Your exchange is supposed to be 4 nice months, so a great tip is to not choose courses that take up way too much time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were generally lower when compared to my courses at KU. I took mainly 300 level courses, which was okay, but definitely easier than what I am used to. As a third year bachelor student, I believe 400 courses are academically more suiting (but I found it really nice that I didn't have to focus too much on school)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is quite different from Denmark, since it resembles our gymnasium quite a lot. For some courses it is mandatory to show up to class, there are quite a lot of assignments, and you are being graded throughout the entire semester. This is often seen by the final exam counting between 30 and 50% of your final grade, whilst the rest is determined based on assignments, participation etc. This was a little stressfull throughout the semester, and I didn't feel nearly as independent as a normally do, but once we reached the finals, it was really nice that you didn't have to study a lot to get an okay grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BIOL 364 Comparative Cardiovascular, Respiratory and Osmoregulatory Physiology
BIOL 260 Fundamentals of Physiology
BIOL 335 Molecular Genetics
BIOL 336 Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Fundamentals of Evolutionary Biology. This is not a classic molecular biomedicine course, but I have been missing some more evolution at KU, so it was really nice being able to do it at UBC. Also, the teacher Wayne was such a great and charismatic teacher.

questions.answer:
It was really expensive to do grocery shopping. 
Phone plan is also expensive in Canada
Expect to use a lot of money on traveling, the area around Vancouver is amazing!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It was a little less expensive going out to eat in Vancouver compared to Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Since I started my exchange while Covid was still going on, not a lot of non-academic opportunities were available from the beginning.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything! UBC rec has a lot of different clubs, involving different sports, languages, clubs related to specific studies as well as a surf club and an outdoor club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Use the aquatic center and sports facilities (badminton, volley, basket) on campus - they are free!
The Varsity Outdoor Club also offers some amazing trips

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Get out of Vancouver, and especially out of Campus. You are surrounded by the most amazing mountains, so use them as much as possible - for skiing, hiking or just going for a drive. 
It is possible to get around by bus, but definitely easier if you have or know someone with a car.
Go to Vancouver Island and spend some time - Tofino is an amazing little surf-town.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Canada is not very far from Denmark culturally so I didn't find it difficult to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use your time in classes if possible!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing was particularly challenging, but you have to get used to tipping when paying for anything, and the very polite lifestyle of the Canadians - they line up very nicely at the bus-stops, so don't just get in front of everybody.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The canadians are very friendly and easygoing, and I always felt really safe, and certain that someone would help me if needed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember to enjoy your time - do not spend too much time and energy on school, there is so much else to experience!
Remember, that life back home goes on as usual. You don't miss out on a lot, so you can just as well focus on yourself and your time in Canada, when you come home, most things are as they were when you left. 
Say yes to any opportunity you are giving. 4 months passes by incredibly fast, so do as much as possible when you can

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you like skiing, remember to buy a season pass for Whistler well in advance, a lot of money is saved!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to fully commit to a different lifestyle for a few months. When on exchange, you don't need to focus on anything besides yourself, and you have so much time to just do whatever you want without any great commitments. Also, I feel super grateful for all of the friends I got in Canada!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It does take quite a lot of courage and planning when going abroad for such a long period, and there are definitely a lot of boring days where you miss everything back home

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
